knowledge_items.title: Inverter does not power up.
knowledge_items.description: Inverter does not power up.
knowledge_items.remedy: Possible cause(s) and corrective action (columns as printed): Power cable is incorrectly wired. Check input wiring Short bar or DCL between [P] and [PD] is disconnected. Install short bar or DCL between [P] and [PD] terminal. Power cable is broken. Check input wiring.

knowledge_items.title: Motor does not start.
knowledge_items.description: Motor does not start.
knowledge_items.remedy: Possible cause(s) and corrective action (columns as printed): Incorrect RUN command source is selected. Check RUN command selection ( A002 ) for correct source. Ex. Terminal (digital input) : 01 Operator (RUN key) : 02 Incorrect frequency source is selected. Check frequency reference selection ( A001 ) for correct source. Ex. Terminal (analog input) : 01 Operator (F001) : 02 Frequency setting is 0 Hz. If frequency reference selection is terminal ( A001 = 01 ), check analog voltage or current signal at [O] or [OI] terminals. If frequency reference selection is operator ( A001 =02), set frequency in F001 . Depending on frequency source, input proper frequency reference. If frequency reference selection is multi-speed operation, set frequency in A020 to A035 and A220 . RUN command is not set to input terminal. If RUN command selection is terminal ( A002 = 01 ), set “forward” ( 00 :FW) or “reverse” ( 01 :RV) to any input terminals. In case of 3-wire control, set “3wire start” ( 20 :STA), “3-wire stop” ( 21 :STP) and “3-wire FW/RV” ( 22 :F/R) to any input terminals. “Multi-step speed reference” ( 02 to 05 :CF1 to CF4)” is (are) set to input terminal(s) and active. Deactivate the input(s), or check the frequency reference parameters associated ( A021 to A035 ). Both FWD and REV input are active. If RUN command source is FWD/REV input, activate either FWD or REV input. Rotation direction limit selection ( b035 ) is enabled. Check b035 . Incorrect input wiring or short bar position Wire inputs correctly and/or install short bar. (ON/OFF status of inputs are monitored in d005 .) Incorrect analog input or variable resistor wiring Wire correctly. In case of analog voltage or variable resistor input, check voltage between [O] and [L] terminal. In case of analog current, check current between current source and [OI] terminal. RUN command source is operator, but input terminal is set to “Force terminal” and active. Deactivate the input. RUN command source is terminal, but input terminal is set to “Force operator” and active. Deactivate the input. Inverter is in trip status. (With ALARM LED and “ E xxx” indication) Reset inverter by STOP/RESET key and check error code.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: 2.  Motor does not start.

knowledge_items.title: Motor does not accelerate to command speed.
knowledge_items.description: Motor does not accelerate to command speed.
knowledge_items.remedy: Possible cause(s) and corrective action (columns as printed): Bad connection of analog wiring. Check the wiring. In case of analog voltage or variable resistor input, check voltage between [O] and [L] terminal. In case of analog current, check current between current source and [OI] terminal. Overload restriction or OC suppression function works. Check the function level. Max. frequency ( A004 ) or upper limit ( A061 / A261 ) is lower than as expected. Check the value. Acceleration time is excessive. Change acceleration time ( F002 / A092 / A292 ). “Multi-speed input(s) ( 02 to 05 :CF1 to CF4)” is (are) set to input terminal(s) and active. Deactivate the input(s). “ 06 :JG” is set to input terminal and the input is active. Deactivate the input. Excess load. Remove excess load. Motor is locked. Unlock the motor.

knowledge_items.title: Specification footnotes
knowledge_items.description: Notes 1-6 for the specification tables: protection method per JEM 1030; applicable motor is a standard 3-phase 4-pole motor; output voltage decreases with supply voltage; overvoltage categories (460-480 VAC category 2, 380-460 VAC category 3); starting torque at rated voltage with 4-pole motor.

details.table: Footnotes for the preceding table and the tables that follow: Note 1 The protection method conforms to JEM 1030. Note 2 The applicable motor refers to a standard 3-phase motor (4p). When using other motors, care must be taken to prevent the rated motor current (50/ 60 Hz) from exceeding the rated output current of the inverter. Note 3 The output voltage decreases as the main supply voltage decreases (except when using the AVR function). In any case, the output voltage cannot exceed the input power supply voltage. Note 4 To operate the motor beyond 50/60 Hz, consult the motor manufacturer for the maximum allowable rotation speed. Note 5 For achieving approved input voltage rating categories: • 460 to 480 VAC - Over-voltage category 2 • 380 to 460 VAC - Over-voltage category 3 To meet the Over-voltage category 3, insert an EN or IEC standard compliant isolation transformer that is earth grounded and star connected (for Low Voltage Directive). Note 6 At the rated voltage when using a standard 3-phase, 4-pole motor.

knowledge_items.title: Specification footnotes (notes 7-12)
knowledge_items.description: Notes 7-12: braking torque via capacitive feedback is the average deceleration torque at the shortest deceleration; frequency command max at 9.8 V / 19.6 mA; derating per carrier frequency; storage temperature is short-term transportation temperature; watt losses are calculated values.

details.table: Note 7 The braking torque via capacitive feedback is the average deceleration torque at the shortest deceleration (stopping from 50/60 Hz as indicated). It is not continuous regenerative braking torque. The average deceleration torque varies with motor loss. This value decreases when operating beyond 50 Hz. If a large regenerative torque is required, the optional regenerative braking unit and a resistor should be used. Note 8 The frequency command is the maximum frequency at 9.8 V for input voltage 0 to 10 VDC, or at 19.6 mA for input current 4 to 20 mA. If this characteristic is not satisfactory for your application, contact your Omron representative. Note 9 If the inverter is operated outside the region shown in the graph in the derating curve, the inverter may be damaged or its service life may be shortened. Set B083 Carrier Frequency Adjustment in accordance with the expected output current level. See derating curve section for the detailed information of the inverter operating range. Note 10 The storage temperature refers to the short-term temperature during transportation. Note 11 Conforms to the test method specified in JIS C0040 (1999). For the model types excluded in the standard specifications, contact your Omron sales representative. Note 12 Watt losses are calculated values based on specification of main semi-conductors. You must take suitable margin when designing cabinet based on these values. Otherwise there is a possibility of heating trouble.

knowledge_items.title: Transmission procedure and query frame
knowledge_items.description: Query is a frame from master to inverter; response is returned only after a query. Frame: header (silent interval), slave address, function code, data, error check, trailer (silent interval). Slave address 0 = broadcast; 250 (FAh) broadcast to 01-09, 251 (FBh) 10-19, 252 (FCh) 20-29, 253 (FDh) 30-39, 254 (FEh) 40-247 (no response, write commands 05h, 06h, 0Fh, 10h only).

knowledge_items.title: CRC and silent interval timing
knowledge_items.description: CRC-16 (X16+X15+X2+1). 3.5 characters (24 bits) of silent interval always required; if shorter the inverter returns no response. Actual transmission latency = silent interval (3.5 characters) + C078.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Modbus-RTU uses CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check) for error checking.

knowledge_items.title: Response and no-response cases
knowledge_items.description: Normal response: loopback returns the query; write commands return the query; read commands return the data with same slave address and function code. On a query error the inverter returns an exception response (function code + 80h). No response when receiving broadcast, on transmission error, slave address mismatch, inter-character interval shorter than 3.5 characters, or invalid data length. Master should use a timer and retransmit.

notes: Printed page = PDF page index - 26 throughout this document (e.g. PDF 115 = printed 89).

Function codes in the Section 3 tables are stored in the PDF text layer as private-use glyphs (U+F0xx = ASCII + 0xF000, e.g. U+F046 U+F030 U+F030 U+F032 = F002); they were decoded programmatically and cross-checked against Appendix C (printed 357-372) and the Modbus listing (printed 316-346), which carry the codes as plain text. No parameter code had to be skipped.

Evidence quotes for Section 3 parameters use the name/description text after the code glyphs so they are verbatim; where a parameter is not described in a Section 3 table (mostly P-group, some b/C items) the cited page is the Modbus register listing or Appendix C line that contains the code.
Defaults are the EU column. A054 default printed as 50 with a second value 40 on the next line in Appendix C; recorded as 50. A082/A282 default printed 230/400 (by voltage class).
Appendix C prints the second-motor speed response code as H005 twice; the Modbus listing shows H205, so H205 is used.

Options were taken from the Section 3 option lists (code ... label) and, where absent or truncated, from the Modbus listing option text. Ranges (min/max) are only filled when the Section 3 wording gives them.

Registers: all Modbus coil (B-4-1) and holding register (B-4-2) rows with a name are listed; high/low word pairs with the same function code are merged into one record. Reserved/unused ranges are omitted. Per-register function codes are not listed in the data tables (function_codes null); supported function codes are in knowledge_items (communication).
Output current monitor d002 (1003h) shows range 0 to 999900 at 0.01 [A], and rotation direction monitor d003 (1004h) shows 0.1 [Hz] in the printed table; copied as printed, looks questionable.
Possible-missing codes reported by check (A230, A400, A215, b140, F101, F011, b066, b068) are references in prose/examples or formula text, not parameters.
A001 option 00 is labelled VR (Digital Operator) in Section 3 but Digital operator in the Modbus listing.
